title: Measuring at the Workbench
cardDescription: Start at the workbench with familiar measuring tools, shape words, and American units of length.
description: Start at the workbench with familiar measuring tools, shape words, and American units of length.
focus: The clues describe tools and the dimensions or directions they identify. Some words name a physical item; others describe a measurement, a mark, or an alignment.
solvingTip: Look for whether the clue asks for a tool, a dimension, a unit, or a mark. Length and depth identify different dimensions. Short measuring terms can help with longer layout words.
words: Straight tool marked with units for measuring length
Flexible measuring strip that can be rolled into a case
Layout tool used to check a right angle
Tool used to check whether a surface is horizontal
True vertical, as checked with a hanging weight
Small indication showing a measured position
Material used to leave a visible temporary layout line
Graphite writing tool used to mark wood
Straight or curved mark traced across a surface
U.S. length unit equal to one-twelfth of a foot
U.S. length unit equal to twelve inches
U.S. length unit equal to three feet
Distance across an object from side to side
Distance from one end of an object to the other
Distance from a front surface to the back or inward
Series of measurement markings on a rule
Following a direct line without a curve

answerNotes.SQUARE: Square names a right-angle checking tool here. It does not ask for the four-sided geometric shape.
answerNotes.LEVEL: A level checks horizontal alignment. Plumb describes true vertical, so the direction being checked matters.
answerNotes.PLUMB: Plumb means vertical in this layout setting. It sounds like plum, the fruit, but has a final b in its spelling.
answerNotes.INCH: Twelve inches make one foot. The clue names the smaller American unit rather than the whole foot.
answerNotes.YARD: A yard equals three feet. It is a length measure here rather than the land around a house.
answerNotes.SCALE: Scale names the measurement markings here. It does not mean a weighing device or a fish covering.

title: Wood and the Saw Cut
cardDescription: Explore wood types, board forms, and the familiar words used to describe a saw and its cut.
description: Explore wood types, board forms, and the familiar words used to describe a saw and its cut.
focus: This puzzle identifies materials and cutting vocabulary through direct descriptions. Some answers name a type of wood; others name a tool part, a cut direction, or material left behind.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names wood, a tool part, or a feature of the cut. A definition may ask for the direction of a cut or the pattern of wood fibers. Short material words can help with longer board forms.
words: Toothed cutting tool used for wood
Flat cutting part of a saw
One pointed cutting projection on a saw blade
Narrow slot or width of material removed by a saw
Opening or separation made by a blade
To saw along the direction of the wood grain
Natural pattern and direction of wood fibers
Saw cut made across the direction of wood grain
Long thick flat piece of timber
Solid fibrous material forming tree trunks and branches
Wood from the tree that produces acorns
Common softwood from an evergreen with bundled needles
Hardwood from the tree associated with syrup production
Aromatic wood often associated with storage chests
Pale wood from a tree often known for peeling bark
Thin sheet of wood applied over another surface
Panel made from joined layers of wood veneer
Fine wood particles left by sawing

answerNotes.KERF: Kerf names the slot made by a saw or the width removed. It is a feature of the cut rather than the tool itself.
answerNotes.RIP: A rip cut follows the grain. Crosscut names a cut across the grain, so direction distinguishes the terms.
answerNotes.GRAIN: Wood grain concerns the fibers and their pattern. It is not a cereal crop in this material clue.
answerNotes.VENEER: Veneer is a thin layer placed over another surface. Plywood is built from multiple wood layers rather than just one decorative face.
answerNotes.PLYWOOD: Plywood consists of bonded veneer layers, commonly with alternating grain direction. The clue asks for the panel material.
answerNotes.SAWDUST: Sawdust is made of fine particles produced during sawing. Scrap instead describes a leftover piece large enough to remain a separate offcut.

title: Joining the Pieces
cardDescription: Bring pieces together through familiar words for fasteners, joints, and the tools that hold or drive them.
description: Bring pieces together through familiar words for fasteners, joints, and the tools that hold or drive them.
focus: The clues identify objects by their shape or job. Some answers name a complete fastener, while others name one part, a joining material, or a holding tool.
solvingTip: Ask whether the clue names a fastener, a fastener part, or a tool. A threaded item and the matching piece turned onto it have different names. Short hardware words can help with longer joining terms.
words: Pointed metal fastener driven into wood
Threaded fastener turned into a material
Threaded fastener commonly secured with a nut
Internally threaded piece turned onto a bolt
Flat ring placed beneath a bolt head or nut
Adhesive used to bond pieces together
Place where two pieces of material meet
Cylindrical rod used to locate or join wood pieces
Short pin fitted into a hole
Tool that temporarily grips pieces together
Bench-mounted gripping tool with opposing jaws
Striking tool commonly used to drive nails
Striking tool with a broad wooden or rubber head
Tool used to turn a screw
Spiral ridge around a screw or bolt
Wider top end of a nail or screw
Long body of a nail beneath its head
Word before hole for a small guiding opening
Jointed hardware allowing a door or lid to swing
Support fixed at an angle beneath a shelf or similar part

answerNotes.NUT: Nut is the threaded hardware piece here. It does not mean a hard-shelled food in this workshop setting.
answerNotes.WASHER: A washer is a flat hardware ring. The clue asks for that small part rather than a laundry machine.
answerNotes.VISE: Vise is the American spelling for the gripping tool. Vice is a different spelling with other meanings in American English.
answerNotes.DOWEL: A dowel is a cylindrical rod used in joining or alignment. It differs from a flat metal bracket.
answerNotes.THREAD: Thread is a spiral fastener ridge in this clue. It is not the sewing strand that shares the spelling.
answerNotes.MALLET: A mallet usually has a broad striking head made from wood, rubber, or another material. That form distinguishes it from a typical nail-driving hammer.

title: The Finishing Touch
cardDescription: Explore finishes through familiar coating names, brush parts, and the words describing a surface.
description: Explore finishes through familiar coating names, brush parts, and the words describing a surface.
focus: This puzzle names finishing materials and tools without giving an application procedure. Clues distinguish appearance, texture, and equipment through everyday definitions.
solvingTip: Look for a coating, a tool part, a texture, or a surface appearance. One clue asks for a coating layer; another asks for one fiber of a spreading tool. Short surface words can help with longer coating terms.
words: Colored coating applied to a surface
Wood-coloring treatment that can leave the grain visible
Clear or tinted protective coating often used on wood
Coating intended to close or protect a surface
Bristled tool used to spread a coating
Cylindrical tool that spreads paint as it turns
Shallow container holding paint for a roller
Part of a paintbrush held in the hand
One stiff fiber in a paintbrush
One layer of paint or another finish
Preparatory coating placed before a finish coat
High-shine appearance of a finished surface
Describing a surface with little or no shine
Degree or quality of surface shine
Natural wood pattern visible beneath some finishes
To smooth a surface with an abrasive material
Even in texture without obvious roughness
No longer wet on the surface
Small hanging or running drop of excess coating
Surface treatment or final appearance of an object

answerNotes.PRIMER: Primer is a preparatory coating. It names a material's role rather than the final color selected for a surface.
answerNotes.MATTE: Matte describes a low-shine surface. Gloss names a high-shine appearance, so the reflection in the clue distinguishes them.
answerNotes.COAT: Coat means a layer of finish here. It is not a garment worn outdoors.
answerNotes.BRISTLE: One bristle is one fiber in a brush. The clue asks for a part rather than the whole tool.
answerNotes.STAIN: Wood stain colors the material while often leaving grain visible. It differs in purpose from an opaque paint layer.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry describes the surface condition in this clue. Surface dryness does not itself specify that a coating has fully cured.

title: A Tidy Tool Bench
cardDescription: Put workshop words in order through familiar containers, storage fixtures, and simple tidying actions.
description: Put workshop words in order through familiar containers, storage fixtures, and simple tidying actions.
focus: The clues follow the places tools are kept and the actions used to arrange them. Some answers name a whole container, while others name a support, a cleaning item, or a tidying action.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue asks for a container, a storage fixture, or an action. A board for hanging tools and an individual curved hanger have different names.
words: Sturdy work surface used for workshop tasks
Handheld implement used to perform a task
Sliding storage compartment beneath a work surface
Horizontal storage board holding tools or boxes
Open container used to group small workshop items
Rigid container used to store supplies
Frame designed to hold tools in an arranged position
Curved hanger used to suspend a tool
Perforated wall panel used with tool hangers
Written marker identifying a storage container's contents
To put tools away for later use
To place boxes or boards one above another
To gather loose floor debris with a broom
Long-handled brush used to clean a floor
Flat receptacle used to collect swept debris
Piece of old cloth used for wiping
Flexible electrical lead attached to a powered tool
Protective container shaped to hold a tool
Part of a storage box grasped for carrying

answerNotes.PEGBOARD: Pegboard has repeated holes for movable hangers. It names the panel rather than an individual hook.
answerNotes.DRAWER: A drawer slides out from a cabinet or bench. A shelf is a stationary support, so the movement helps identify it.
answerNotes.SORT: Sort means group items by type or another feature. It is an arranging action rather than the name of a container.
answerNotes.STACK: Stack is used as a verb for placing things above one another. The clue does not ask for one particular box.
answerNotes.DUSTPAN: A dustpan collects debris gathered by a broom. It differs from the brush that moves the debris.
answerNotes.CASE: Case is a protective tool container here. It does not mean a legal matter or a grammatical category.
